clue.text: One very quiet old doctor occupying seat in theatre

indicators.note: the run of short pieces sits inside the word for seat, as tenants occupy a home

parts.note: a seat can be a home, as in a family seat
one is the Roman numeral I
pp, pianissimo, is the musical marking for very quiet

explanation.surface: An elderly, silent doctor has taken a seat at the theatre.
explanation.definitionFit: A hippodrome was originally a racecourse, and the name is now used for many music halls and variety venues.

clue.text: Mass in Greek?

parts.note: not a church service: the masses, the common people, expressed in a Greek phrase meaning 'the many'

explanation.surface: A question about which language a church Mass is said in.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mass' suggests a religious service; here it means the masses, and the Greek phrase used in English for them.
explanation.definitionFit: The Greek phrase means 'the many' and is used in English for ordinary people, the masses.

clue.text: For which one must interrupt work?

definitions.text: For which one must interrupt work?

parts.words: For which one must interrupt work?
parts.note: read as the leisure that can only be had by breaking off from one's labour

explanation.surface: A riddle about what makes you stop working.
explanation.definitionFit: Recreation is the opposite of labour, so taking time for fun means pausing one's job.

clue.text: Bird call formerly heard at Edgbaston, note appearing strangely harmonic

parts.words: Bird call formerly heard at Edgbaston
parts.note: Dickie Bird, a famous retired cricket umpire, called 'over' at the end of each set of six balls; Edgbaston is a Birmingham cricket ground

indicators.note: the letters of note appear in a strange new order

explanation.surface: A birdsong once heard at a cricket ground has an odd harmonic quality.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bird' is not a songbird but the umpire Dickie Bird, who has retired, hence 'formerly'. 'appearing strangely' rearranges NOTE to TONE.
explanation.definitionFit: In acoustics a harmonic is a higher tone sounding above the fundamental, the same as an upper partial.

clue.text: Pipe is coming between King and Queen

indicators.note: the word is sits between the letters for king and queen

parts.note: R, for Rex, is Latin for king
ER, Elizabeth Regina, stands for queen

explanation.surface: A pipe is placed between the king and queen, like a royal chaperone.
explanation.definitionFit: In plumbing a vertical supply pipe running up through a building is called this.

clue.text: Young lady, one on Disappearing cannabis found in ethnically mixed area

annotationWithheld.why: the clue as held reads 'Young lady, one on Disappearing cannabis found in ethnically mixed area': after MISS + I + ON the rest of 5-down's clue, holding its definition, is replaced by 6-down's clue, and no print or search gives the missing words
annotationWithheld.clue: Young lady, one on Disappearing cannabis found in ethnically mixed area

clue.text: Disappearing cannabis found in ethnically mixed area

parts.note: something melting is dwindling away, disappearing
pot is slang for cannabis

explanation.surface: Drugs that vanish turn up in a multicultural neighbourhood.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase describes a place where many peoples and cultures blend together.

clue.text: Splendid agent recruited by small business on the way up

indicators.note: in a down clue the assembled letters are read from bottom to top
the agent is taken inside the business, as a new hire is

parts.note: bus. is the short form of business
a rep, a sales representative, is an agent

explanation.surface: A fine salesman is hired by a growing little firm.
explanation.walkthrough: 'recruited by' puts REP inside BUS to give BREPUS; 'on the way up' turns it round in this down entry.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words mean excellent or magnificent.

clue.text: To explain working of clue one needs time

indicators.note: the letters of clue are worked into a new order

parts.note: one is the Roman numeral I
a date is a point in time

explanation.surface: Solving a crossword clue takes patience if you want to explain it.
explanation.definitionFit: To make something clear is to clarify or spell it out.

clue.text: Indifferent staff officer sits outside map-making department

indicators.note: the officer's letters surround those of the department

parts.note: SO is the abbreviation for staff officer
the OS, Ordnance Survey, is Britain's national mapping agency

explanation.surface: An uninterested officer waits outside the mapping office.
explanation.definitionFit: Indifferent here means mediocre, only middling.

clue.text: Quake in Turkey with repercussion for Italian city

parts.note: TR is the international vehicle code for Turkey

indicators.note: a repercussion rebounds, so the city's name comes back in reverse

parts.note: Rome is the Italian capital

explanation.surface: An earthquake in Turkey sends aftershocks to Italy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'with repercussion' turns ROME back to EMOR.
explanation.definitionFit: A small earthquake or shaking of the ground is the same thing.

clue.text: Look hard, making slight reduction to angle — you'll see asteroid

indicators.note: a small cut takes the last letter off the word for look hard

parts.note: to stare is to look hard
to angle is to fish with rod and line

explanation.surface: Stare closely and narrow the angle of your telescope to spot an asteroid.
explanation.walkthrough: 'making slight reduction to' drops the E of STARE. 'Asteroid' means star-shaped: zoologists call starfish asteroids, after the class Asteroidea.
explanation.definitionFit: Asteroid is a zoological term for a member of the sea creatures' star-shaped class.

clue.text: Heretical view offered by male seen on terrace with old trollop

parts.note: he is the male pronoun
Ter. is the address abbreviation for terrace
doxy is an old word for a mistress or loose woman

explanation.surface: A man on a terraced street with a disreputable old woman holds unorthodox opinions.
explanation.definitionFit: Heresy is a belief at odds with accepted doctrine, the opposite of orthodoxy.

clue.text: Sexually attractive woman's hairstyle, swept back, that is worn by student

indicators.note: the hairstyle is brushed backwards, so its letters are reversed

parts.note: a bun is a hairstyle

indicators.note: the student is inside the abbreviation for that is, as clothes are worn

parts.note: i.e. abbreviates id est, that is
L is the learner sign, for a student

explanation.surface: An attractive woman with her hair swept back is admired by a student.
explanation.walkthrough: 'swept back' turns BUN to NUB; 'worn by' puts L inside IE.
explanation.definitionFit: Used of a young woman, it means marriageable or sexually desirable.

clue.text: Computer facility one entrant misused

parts.note: one is the Roman numeral I

indicators.note: the letters of entrant are put to the wrong use, rearranged

explanation.surface: A newcomer misuses a computer.
explanation.definitionFit: An organisation's private internal network is a computing resource.

clue.text: Girl leaving when 'hourglass' gets bandied about, not yet having divine shape?

indicators.note: the remaining letters are tossed around into a new order
the girl departs from the word hourglass

parts.note: a lass is a girl

explanation.surface: A girl leaves as the word 'hourglass' is thrown about, the figure yet to be shaped.
explanation.walkthrough: 'leaving' takes LASS from HOURGLASS to leave HOURG; with WHEN, 'gets bandied about' rearranges them. The definition echoes Hamlet: 'There's a divinity that shapes our ends, rough-hew them how we will.'
explanation.definitionFit: Something only roughly shaped awaits finishing, as Hamlet says a divinity gives final shape to what we roughly carve.

clue.text: Unstable new currency leads to nervous reaction

parts.note: the euro is a currency
a tic is an involuntary twitch

explanation.surface: A shaky new currency sets off a nervous twitch in the markets.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone emotionally unstable is anxious and obsessive.

clue.text: If prince meets poet journalist tags along

parts.note: Ovid was a Roman poet
ED, editor, is the usual crossword journalist

explanation.surface: Suppose a prince meets a poet with a reporter following.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words introduce a condition: on condition that.

clue.text: Conquer viral skin problem in leg (about to be excised)

indicators.note: the shortened skin complaint goes inside the word for leg

parts.note: the on side, also called the leg side, is a half of a cricket field

indicators.note: the word for about is cut out of the skin problem

parts.note: a verruca is a wart caused by a virus
ca., circa, means about

explanation.surface: Defeating a viral wart on the leg means cutting it out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to be excised' removes CA from VERRUCA to leave VERRU; 'in' puts it inside ON. In cricket the leg side is also the on side.
explanation.definitionFit: To overrun a country is to invade and occupy it.

clue.text: Foreign resident Academician at Oxford, with attitude

parts.note: A is an abbreviation for Academician, as in ARA
a student up is in residence at university
an air is a manner or attitude

explanation.surface: An overseas academic at Oxford is rather full of themselves.
explanation.walkthrough: In British usage you are 'up' at Oxford or Cambridge while studying there.
explanation.definitionFit: A young person from abroad living with a family and helping with childcare.

clue.text: A large group touring Spain, encountering a simple form of life

indicators.note: the crowd goes round Spain, encircling its letter

parts.note: a mob is a large crowd
E is the international vehicle code for Spain

explanation.surface: A big tour party in Spain meets a primitive organism.
explanation.definitionFit: This single-celled organism is a textbook example of primitive life.

clue.text: Jacket lining torn or gone missing in plant

indicators.note: the jacket lines what is left of torn, sitting inside it
the word or disappears from torn

parts.note: a reefer is a short double-breasted jacket

explanation.surface: A jacket's lining is ripped or has vanished in a factory.
explanation.walkthrough: 'gone missing' removes OR from TORN to leave TN; 'lining' puts REEFER inside. 'Plant' looks like a factory but is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A large tropical fern with a trunk-like stem is a plant.

clue.text: Vessel, form of ferry

indicators.note: a different form of the word ferry, its letters rearranged

explanation.surface: A ship that is a kind of ferry.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Vessel' suggests a boat, as does 'ferry', but this is a cooking vessel.
explanation.definitionFit: A deep pan for cooking food in fat is a kitchen vessel.

clue.text: Penelope's handiwork by day requiring hours to unravel?

indicators.note: the letters of hours are unpicked into a new order

explanation.surface: Odysseus's wife wove by day and spent hours of night undoing it.
explanation.walkthrough: In the Odyssey, Penelope delayed her suitors by weaving her father-in-law's burial cloth by day and unravelling it each night. 'to unravel' rearranges HOURS.
explanation.definitionFit: Penelope's weaving was a burial cloth for Laertes, which she promised to finish before remarrying.

clue.text: Opponent making a no-trump intervention originally

parts.note: NT is the bridge abbreviation for no-trump

indicators.note: the first letter of intervention is taken

explanation.surface: A bridge opponent opens with a no-trump bid.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone against a proposal is an objector.

clue.text: Wild revel for gypsies? Not entirely

indicators.note: only part of the words for gypsies is used, the answer lying inside them

explanation.surface: A wild party, but only partly for travelling folk.
explanation.definitionFit: A drunken, riotous celebration.

clue.text: Fashionable hat, not quite round, in Texas something inflammatory?

indicators.note: the pieces go inside the abbreviation for Texas

parts.note: TX is the postal abbreviation for Texas
in means fashionable

indicators.note: the hat's name loses its last letter

parts.note: a derby is a bowler hat
O is round in shape

explanation.surface: A stylish hat, not quite round, in Texas causes a stir.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not quite' cuts DERBY to DERB; IN + DERB + O go inside TX.
explanation.definitionFit: A box of dry kindling for lighting fires, and figuratively a volatile situation.

clue.text: Violation of law in French court case

parts.note: an action is a lawsuit

explanation.surface: A breach of the law tried in a French court.
explanation.definitionFit: A breach or offence against a rule.
